8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: 'His servants / His slaves / His worshippers' — ʿibād are those who serve and worship; with the attached pronoun it denotes the servants belonging to Him (Allah), i.e., humankind or His devotees.
9.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel is the genitive case, typically appearing after a preposition or in a possessive ('of') link; the pronoun names the one to whom the servants belong.

10.meaning: And He measures out, restricts, straitens, or apportions sparingly; to set a fixed measure to provision so as to limit it. The same verb can also mean to have power and to determine.
10.grammar: The prefix 'wa' means 'and'. The core is a present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular; 'ya-' marks 'he/it', and the final '-u' marks the plain indicative — an ongoing or habitual action ('he restricts / keeps measuring out'). The root joins the ideas of measuring, decreeing, and having power.

11.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
11.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

12.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

13.meaning: To spend, expend, or disburse — to lay out wealth or resources, often for the sake of others or a cause.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb from a causative pattern (to cause wealth to go out, i.e. to spend). The ending -tum marks a masculine plural doer, 'you all'.
13.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, to expend; expenditure

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

15.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
15.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
15.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

16.meaning: A two-part phrase: the connector 'then / so' plus the standalone pronoun 'he / it,' used to point back and resume with 'then he…' or 'so it…'
16.grammar: The connector 'fa' ('then/so') plus the detached subject pronoun 'huwa' ('he/it'), 3rd-person masculine singular. Both are indeclinable, with no case ending; the pronoun typically begins or emphasizes a statement about 'he/it.'

18.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
18.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

19.meaning: 'Best / the best (of)' — superior to all others in goodness, excellence, or worth; the finest in its class.
19.grammar: khayr functions as a comparative/superlative noun ('better / best'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also opens a possessive phrase ('the best OF …').
19.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or best

20.meaning: 'The providers / the sustainers' — those who supply provision and the means of life; a plural describing the doers of the act of providing.
20.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural. The pattern fāʿil ('rāziq') names the one performing the act; the '-īna' ending marks a masculine plural in the object/genitive state (the form used after prepositions, as a non-subject, or after certain particles).
20.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide sustenance, livelihood, provision

1.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'He gathers them' or 'He will assemble them' — to collect and herd people together into one place, as in the great mustering of creation.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The stem-final -u is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement of fact (and, of future events, what will certainly occur). The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural).
2.root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r) — to gather, herd together, muster

3.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
3.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.
3.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — gathering, joining, bringing together

4.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
4.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

5.meaning: 'He says' or 'he is saying' — the act of speaking or uttering words. The imperfect tense conveys an ongoing, habitual, or present/future action.
5.grammar: Imperfect (present/future) verb, third person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he', the stem qūl carries the meaning 'say', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement (as opposed to a subjunctive -a or jussive sukūn used after certain particles).

6.meaning: 'To the angels' — the preposition 'to / for' joined to the definite plural 'the angels', the beings created of light who serve and obey.
6.grammar: A preposition + the definite article + a noun. The prefix li- ('to / for') places the noun in the genitive state, shown by the final -i. The l- is the definite article 'the'. The -at- is a feminine/collective ending on the plural 'angels'. So the genitive -i here is triggered by the preposition 'to / for'.

7.meaning: Are these (people)? — a near-demonstrative 'these' carried into a question. It points to a group close at hand while the opening hamza turns the pointing into a query.
7.grammar: The plural near-demonstrative 'these' (hāʾulāʾ) prefixed by the interrogative hamza ('are these…?'). Demonstratives like this are fixed forms that do not change for case the way ordinary nouns do; the closing -i here is the connecting vowel that smooths it into what follows.

9.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
9.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

10.meaning: Means 'they worship / they serve in devotion' — a present-tense verb for the ongoing act of worship: humble service, obedience, and devotion directed to a deity.
10.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending means 'they (masculine plural) do …'. The full -ūna ending also marks the verb as a plain statement of fact (indicative), as opposed to a shortened form used after certain particles.

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: 'Glory be to You / how far above all flaw You are' — a set exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of any imperfection, partner, or unworthy attribute, paired with 'You.'
2.grammar: A verbal noun, subḥān ('glorification, utter freedom from imperfection'), bound to the attached pronoun -ka, 'You/Your' (one masculine addressee). It stands in the accusative (-a ending) as the exclamatory object of an understood verb ('I declare Your absolute glory') — a fixed formula of praise.
2.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — glorifying, declaring (Allah) free of all imperfection

3.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
3.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

4.meaning: Our protector / guardian / ally — the wali: a near and supporting friend who takes charge of one's affairs, protects, and stands as patron; joined to a pronoun marking the relationship as 'ours.' It stands as a predicate ('You are our protector').
4.grammar: A noun with the -u (nominative) ending, the form used for the subject or for the predicate naming a thing (as in 'You are our protector'), followed by the possessive suffix -nā ('our'). The initial waw is the first letter of the root, not a conjunction.
4.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, friendship, guardianship and patronage

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: 'Apart from them / besides them / below them'. The base word 'dūn' marks something other than or short of a reference point; with 'them' attached it means 'other than those people' or 'lower/nearer than them'.

parts.en: genitive ending (after this word, before the pronoun)

6.grammar: An adverb/preposition of relation ('apart from, besides, short of') with the attached pronoun -him ('them', masculine plural). The -i vowel is the genitive linking the word to the pronoun; the form -him (with i-vowel) is the regular shape the pronoun takes after a genitive/'i' sound.

7.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

8.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
8.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

9.meaning: Means 'they worship / they serve in devotion' — a present-tense verb for the ongoing act of worship: humble service, obedience, and devotion directed to a deity.
9.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending means 'they (masculine plural) do …'. The full -ūna ending also marks the verb as a plain statement of fact (indicative), as opposed to a shortened form used after certain particles.

10.meaning: The jinn — a class of unseen beings created from smokeless fire, possessing free will and accountability like humans, capable of both good and evil. The word denotes that which is hidden or concealed from ordinary sight.
10.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative ending, marking it as the object of a verb or as a noun following certain particles.

11.meaning: Most of them / the greater part of them — the noun 'akthar' (the greater number, the majority), built on a comparative/superlative pattern of k-th-r ('much/many'), with the pronoun 'them'.
11.grammar: A noun in possessive (genitive) construction: 'aktharu' ('the most of') plus the attached pronoun '-hum' ('them') yields 'most of them'. The '-u' on 'akthar' is the nominative ending, typical when this phrase serves as the subject.
11.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, numerous

12.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
12.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

1.meaning: So / then — the day; a connective particle joined to the noun 'the day.' It links to what precedes (drawing a consequence or sequence, 'so / then') and names the day.
1.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connector meaning 'so / then,' marking a result or sequence. al- is 'the.' The final -a is the accusative case, which often marks a direct object or, with time-words like 'day,' an adverbial sense ('on the day').

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: He owns / possesses / has power over — a verb meaning to have ownership, control, or authority over something, to be able to dispose of it as one wills.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a 3rd-person masculine singular subject ('he') and ongoing/future action. The final -u marks the indicative mood (a plain statement). The verb spans ownership, possession, and the power or authority to control and dispose of a thing.
3.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — ownership, dominion, possessing and holding sway

4.meaning: A phrase meaning 'some of you' or 'one part of you'. It singles out a portion of an addressed group, often paired with 'to/for another' to express a reciprocal relationship within that group.
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'a part/some' carrying the -u ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or doer in its clause. The attached -kum means 'of you all' (plural), so the whole means 'some part of you'.
4.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, some

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to some' or 'for another part'. It marks the recipient or counterpart in a reciprocal pairing, the 'other side' that 'some of you' relate to.
5.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') attached to the noun 'a part/some'. The -in ending is genitive with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'): the genitive case is required after the preposition, and the tanwīn marks the noun as indefinite ('a part', not 'the part').

7.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
7.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

8.meaning: Harm / injury / hurt — that which damages or causes detriment; an affliction or adversity.
8.grammar: A noun. The final -an is 'nunation' (tanwīn) marking it as indefinite ('some harm / a harm'), and its -a vowel signals the accusative case — the ending typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
8.root: ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r) — harm, injury, damage, the opposite of benefit

10.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
10.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

11.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
11.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

12.meaning: Taste! / experience it firsthand — a command to undergo and feel something directly, as one tastes food. Often used of being made to feel a consequence.
12.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group: 'taste!' The -ū ending marks the addressee as masculine plural ('you all'). From a hollow root whose middle letter appears as a long ū in this form.
12.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste, to experience directly

13.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
13.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

14.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
14.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

15.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
15.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

16.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
16.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

17.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
17.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

18.meaning: You (a group) deny, reject as false, or treat as a lie — to actively brand something or someone untrue rather than merely doubting.

parts.en: you treat as a lie / deny

18.grammar: A present-tense Form II verb (the doubled, intensive pattern), giving the sense of firmly charging something with falsehood. The stem alone is 2nd-person singular; the '-ūna' ending adds plurality, so the 't-' prefix with that ending marks 'you all' (second person masculine plural) acting now or habitually. The '-ūna' (not '-ū') shows the verb stands in its plain, unaltered present state.
18.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, be false; to deny, call a lie

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: It is being recited or read aloud — said of verses or scripture conveyed by voice, in an ongoing or repeated manner.

parts.en: recite/read aloud (passive stem, root letters t-l + long ā)

2.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) passive verb in the third person feminine singular ('it/she is recited'). The tu- prefix marks both the present tense and the passive voice ('is being …-ed'), so the doer is unnamed and the focus is on what undergoes the action. The stem -tlā keeps the second root consonant (t) and ends in a long ā written with ى, the shape a weak-final (defective) root takes when no further ending is attached.
2.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

3.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
3.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
3.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: Our signs / verses — 'āyāt' are tokens, proofs, and miraculous indications that point to a deeper truth, and also the verses of revelation; with 'Our' it refers to such signs ascribed to Allah.
4.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs, verses') with the attached possessive 'our' = -nā. The -u vowel before the pronoun marks the subject/naming case, the form a noun takes as the doer or topic of a sentence ('Our signs [are/do...]').
4.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token, miraculous indication

5.meaning: Clear, manifest, self-evident — the feminine plural of 'bayyin', describing things that are plainly evident and make matters distinct; an intensive adjective implying something that clarifies and is itself unmistakable.
5.grammar: A sound feminine plural adjective. The '-in' (nunation) ending marks it indefinite and in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case, so it agrees with an indefinite feminine plural noun it describes ('clear ___').
5.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct, evident; to make plain

6.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
8.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: A man; an adult male human being.
10.grammar: A singular noun marked indefinite ('a man'). The final -un (tanwīn) combines the -u nominative case-ending — typically marking the doer or subject of a sentence — with the -n that signals indefiniteness ('a man' rather than 'the man').

11.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills / wants / intends / desires'. It expresses the act of willing or purposing something, from the root of will and intent.
11.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb in the causative (Form IV) pattern. The yu- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'), and the final -u marks the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact). It is transitive, normally taking an object (what is willed).
11.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want; (this form) to will, intend, desire

12.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
12.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

14.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
14.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

15.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

15.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

16.meaning: "he worships / he serves devotedly" — the present-tense act of worship by a single "he" subject.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a single masculine "he" subject; the final -u is the indicative present, expressing an ongoing, habitual, or general action.

17.meaning: Your fathers / forefathers / parents; the plural 'fathers' joined to a 'your (plural)' possessor, denoting the male ancestors or, more broadly, the parents of a group.
17.grammar: A broken plural noun ('fathers') with the attached possessor -kum ('your', addressing several people). The -u case-vowel before the suffix is nominative, typically marking the word as the doer or subject of a sentence. The ending -kum specifically addresses a group of males or a mixed group.

18.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
18.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

19.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
19.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

20.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
20.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

21.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
21.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

24.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
24.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

25.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
25.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

26.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
26.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
26.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

27.meaning: 'To/for the truth' — al-ḥaqq is that which is real, true, established, and rightfully due: reality as it actually is, the right that is owed, and truth as opposed to falsehood. With the prefix it means 'to the truth' or 'for the truth'.

parts.en: truth / reality / what is rightfully due

27.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') attached to the definite noun al-ḥaqq ('the truth'). The -i ending is genitive, the case regularly required after a preposition such as li-.
27.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, real, established, rightfully due

28.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the point that' something occurred — pointing to the moment a past event took place and often implying that one thing happened upon the completion of another. In other uses it can carry the sense of 'not yet'.
28.grammar: A particle (a small connecting word), not a noun or verb, so it has no case or tense ending. It introduces a clause and links it in time to another event — most often 'when / as soon as' a past action happened.

29.meaning: To come to, to arrive at someone; the act of something or someone reaching or presenting itself to a person. A core verb for arrival and the coming of events, messengers, or messages.
29.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it came') — the -a ending marks a completed act by a single masculine subject. The attached -hum is the object 'them,' the ones reached by the coming.

30.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
30.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

31.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
31.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

32.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
32.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

33.meaning: Magic / sorcery — the working of illusions or hidden powers to deceive perception or affect people; by extension, anything dazzling that distorts how things truly are.
33.grammar: A singular noun. The final -un (nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a/some magic') and in the nominative case — the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence or after the verb 'to be'.

34.meaning: Clear, plain, and self-evident; that which makes things manifest. The form carries an active sense: not merely 'clear in itself' but 'making clear,' something that openly displays its nature and leaves no ambiguity.
34.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word) on the form mufʿil, meaning 'one who/that which makes [something] clear.' The final -un is the indefinite nominative ending ('a …'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: We gave them / We granted them; a completed act of bestowing or providing, done by a "we" subject and directed to a group as recipients.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning "to give/grant." The attached -nā marks the subject as "we" (the doer), and the attached -hum marks "them" as the recipients/object. The form states a completed action.
2.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (in this form) to bring, give, grant

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
6.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

7.meaning: We sent / dispatched. From the causative verb meaning to send forth or commission, especially the sending of messengers; with 'We' as the subject.
7.grammar: Past/perfect verb in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send', 1st person plural ('we'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending 'we' on a completed action. The perfect tense presents the sending as accomplished and complete.

8.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
8.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
8.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: Before (someone), prior to them, earlier than them — an adverb of time/place meaning 'preceding' or 'in front of'.
9.grammar: A noun used adverbially in the accusative, shown by the -a before the suffix. The attached -ka ('you', masculine singular) is genitive as the possessor, giving 'before you / prior to you'.
9.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; priority

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: One who warns; a giver of warning who alerts people to danger or coming consequences. It can name a person (a warner) or function as an intensive description (one who warns earnestly).
11.grammar: An active-participle-like noun on the faʿīl pattern, meaning 'a warner.' The ending -in is indefinite ('a warner,' not 'the warner') and genitive, the case used after a preposition or when a noun is linked to a preceding noun as a possessor or specifier.

1.meaning: And/but he denied, called (something) a lie, treated as false. The doubled middle consonant marks an intensive verb: to vigorously reject something as untrue, to give it the lie.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he ...ed'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending. The doubled middle letter (form II, shown by the shadda) makes it intensive/transitive: actively rejecting something as false; the transliteration 'kadhdhaba' doubles the 'dh' to reflect this. The prefixed wa- means 'and' or, in contrast, 'but'.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
3.root: — (preposition)

4.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
4.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
4.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

5.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

6.meaning: They reached / attained — to arrive at a point, age, or limit; the verb conveys coming to and fully attaining a certain stage.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a masculine group). So the form denotes a completed action: 'they reached / attained.'
6.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — reaching, attaining, arriving at a limit or goal

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: We gave them / We granted them; a completed act of bestowing or providing, done by a "we" subject and directed to a group as recipients.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning "to give/grant." The attached -nā marks the subject as "we" (the doer), and the attached -hum marks "them" as the recipients/object. The form states a completed action.
9.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (in this form) to bring, give, grant

12.meaning: So how? / Then in what manner or state? — kayfa is the interrogative 'how', asking after the manner, condition or circumstance of something. With the prefixed 'so/then' it introduces a question following from what precedes, often expressing wonder or warning.
12.grammar: An interrogative particle ('how') carrying the connective prefix fa- ('so / then'), which links it to a preceding statement as a consequence or follow-up. As a particle, kayfa is indeclinable: its fixed final -a is not a case ending and does not change.

13.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

13.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
2.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

6.meaning: You stand / uphold — you rise to maintain something, carry it out with firmness and justice. The verb carries the sense of establishing and being upright in a duty.
6.grammar: Present-tense Form I verb, second-person masculine plural, in the subjunctive/jussive mood: the bare -ū ending (indicative -ūna minus the final -na) typically appears after particles meaning 'that', 'to', or 'so that'. It denotes the act of rising up to perform or maintain.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, establish, uphold

7.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
7.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

8.meaning: In twos — two at a time, or two each. A distributive numeral meaning 'two by two'.
8.grammar: A distributive numeral built from the root for 'two', meaning 'two apiece' or 'in pairs'. It has a fixed ending (long -ā) and does not change for case; it is also diptote (resisting the usual indefinite -n ending). It conveys taking things in groups of two.

10.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
10.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

12.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

15.meaning: Madness / possession by jinn — a state of being overtaken or deranged, mind unsettled as if seized by an unseen agency. The term names insanity in the sense of one's reason being disturbed.
15.grammar: A noun. The ending -in is genitive and indefinite (the 'tanwīn' n-sound = 'a/any'); the genitive case appears after prepositions, in possessive links, or in certain negated constructions. The word derives from the same root as the hidden, concealed jinn — madness being conceived as the mind 'covered over'.
15.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide (hence the hidden jinn and a clouded mind)

16.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
16.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

17.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
17.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

18.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
18.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

19.meaning: A warner — one who gives warning, alerting people to impending danger or consequence so they may take heed. It names the agent who delivers such an admonition.
19.grammar: A noun/adjective on the intensive agent-pattern (faʿīl), denoting one who does something fully or by office — a 'warner'. The ending -un is nominative and indefinite ('a warner'); the nominative marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate, so this typically stands as 'is a warner' or 'a warner (came)'.
19.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution, give notice of danger

20.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
20.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

21.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
21.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
21.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

22.meaning: The two hands; figuratively "front, presence, fore-part." In the phrase "between the two hands of" it idiomatically means "in front of, ahead of, in advance of."
22.grammar: A dual noun ("two hands") in its connected form. The -ay ending is the dual in the genitive/accusative state and signals that it is linked to a following noun ("the two hands OF …"); the final -n of the dual drops because it is joined to what follows.

23.meaning: A punishment / torment — painful chastisement or suffering imposed as a penalty. The word names the punishment itself, stated indefinitely ('a punishment').
23.grammar: A noun, 'punishment/torment'. The final -in (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and genitive in case — the form used after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of a punishment').

24.meaning: An adjective meaning 'strong, mighty, intense, severe, firm' — describing something powerful and hard to overcome.
24.grammar: Singular indefinite adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The '-in' ending marks it indefinite and genitive, agreeing with an indefinite genitive noun it describes ('a strong …').
24.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, firm, severe

3.meaning: I asked you — a past-tense act of requesting, demanding, or seeking something from a group of people, whether a question posed or a favour sought.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-tu' ending means the speaker did it ('I asked'), and the attached '-kum' is the object ('… you', a group). Together they frame a completed request made by one person to many.
3.root: س-ا-ل (s-ʾ-l) — asking, requesting, questioning

5.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — payment earned in return for work, effort, or service, whether earthly compensation or divine reward.
5.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn) marks it as genitive and indefinite, the form a noun typically takes after a preposition, or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of a reward').
5.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for effort

6.meaning: A two-part phrase: the connector 'then / so' plus the standalone pronoun 'he / it,' used to point back and resume with 'then he…' or 'so it…'
6.grammar: The connector 'fa' ('then/so') plus the detached subject pronoun 'huwa' ('he/it'), 3rd-person masculine singular. Both are indeclinable, with no case ending; the pronoun typically begins or emphasizes a statement about 'he/it.'

7.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

8.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
8.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

9.meaning: My reward, my wage, my recompense — the payment or return that is due specifically to the speaker for what they have done.
9.grammar: A singular noun with the attached pronoun '-iya' ('my'). When the possessive '-ī/-iya' is joined, it stands in place of the usual case-vowel, so the noun reads simply as 'my reward', the thing belonging to the speaker.
9.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for effort

11.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
11.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
11.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
13.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

15.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
15.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

16.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
16.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
16.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

17.meaning: A witness — one who sees and observes directly and can testify to what is true; also carries the sense of an ever-watchful observer.
17.grammar: An intensive descriptive noun (pattern 'faʿīl') meaning one who witnesses fully and constantly. The '-un' ending is nominative and indefinite: the nominative typically marks the subject or predicate ('is a witness'), and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
2.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

3.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
3.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

5.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
5.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
5.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

6.meaning: Great Knower / All-Knowing — an intensive form meaning one who knows utterly and completely, especially of hidden things; a possessor of total knowledge.
6.grammar: An intensive noun of the 'faʿʿāl' pattern, expressing knowledge to the highest degree ('one who knows all things'). The final -u is the nominative case; the word commonly stands in construct with a following noun, meaning 'the All-Knower OF …'.

7.meaning: The unseen / the hidden things — the plural of that which is concealed or absent from perception: secrets, mysteries, all that lies beyond the reach of the senses.
7.grammar: A plural noun made definite by 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition.
7.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — to be hidden, absent, unseen

2.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

3.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
3.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
3.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

4.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
4.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
4.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

6.meaning: A noun/active participle meaning 'the false, the vain, that which is baseless or void.' It denotes falsehood — what has no reality, no truth, and no lasting substance, the opposite of what is true and established.
6.grammar: The article al- makes it definite ('the'). The word is an active participle on the pattern fā'il ('that which is …'), here 'that which is null/false.' The final -u is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject (the doer) of a sentence.
6.root: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — to be false, vain, void, come to nothing

7.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
