6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

7.meaning: 'Myself / my own soul'. The word nafs means a self, soul, person or inner being; with the attached 'my' it points to the speaker's own self.
7.grammar: Noun plus the attached possessor -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' suffix replaces the case-ending, so the noun's grammatical role (subject, object, or after a preposition) is read from context rather than from a final short vowel.

8.meaning: And if — joins a clause and introduces a condition ('if such-and-such happens, then …').
8.grammar: The connective wa ('and') plus the conditional particle in ('if'). 'In' sets up a condition whose fulfilment triggers a result clause. Its normally silent final consonant here carries a helping vowel -i to ease pronunciation before the next word; this vowel is not a case ending.

10.meaning: A chain of small words meaning roughly 'so/then, by/through what...' — introducing a result and pointing to the means or cause of something.
10.grammar: A cluster of three particles. The fa- links to what precedes as a consequence ('so, then'); bi- ('by/through/with') indicates the means or cause and governs a genitive; mā here serves as 'what / that which' (and is often partly redundant, adding a nuance of emphasis or vagueness). Together: 'so, by/through that which...'

11.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he inspires / reveals / whispers secretly'. Its core sense is conveying a message swiftly and covertly into someone's mind or heart — whether divine revelation or hidden suggestion.
11.grammar: A Form IV present-tense verb from a root whose final letter is a weak 'y'. The yu- prefix marks a third-person singular masculine subject ('he'), and the final long -ī is the weak root letter showing through; the verb is in the indicative (an ongoing or habitual act of inspiring/revealing).
11.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to inspire, reveal, suggest swiftly and secretly

12.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
12.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'

13.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
13.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

14.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
14.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

15.meaning: All-Hearing / ever-hearing — one who hears completely and perfectly, missing nothing of what is uttered or whispered; an intensive form stressing the fullness of the quality. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
15.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a constant, perfect quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is all-hearing").

16.meaning: Near, close, at hand — close in distance, time, or relationship; readily accessible.
16.grammar: A singular masculine adjective on the intensive paradigm faʿīl, meaning 'near/close'. The ending -un (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('near') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate describing a subject.

1.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

2.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'you see, you behold, you perceive (with the eye)' — and by extension, to come to know or regard something as being a certain way.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single 'you' (the ta- prefix marks second-person masculine singular). It comes from a weak root whose final letter appears as the long -ā vowel. Standing without a following negative or subjunctive particle, it reads as a plain present-tense statement.
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʼ-y) — seeing, perceiving, forming a view

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

5.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
5.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: 'Near / soon / close' — qarīb denotes nearness in place or time, hence 'close at hand' or 'shortly,' or one who is near/related.
10.grammar: An adjective/noun on the fa'īl pattern meaning 'near.' The -in ending is the genitive case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n,' the form taken after a preposition or in an 'of …' relationship with a preceding noun.
10.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, draw close; nearness

1.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they said / spoke / uttered'. It denotes the act of speaking and voicing words.
1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action, built on a hollow (weak-middle) root, so the middle root-letter appears as the long vowel -ā-. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they said'). The wa- means 'and'. (The final silent alif is a spelling convention after plural -ū.)
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter (hollow/weak-middle root)

2.meaning: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.

3.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
3.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

5.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
5.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: Far, distant, or remote — in space, time, or figuratively (as in being far from the truth or from guidance).
9.grammar: An adjective in the intensive/quality paradigm. The -in ending marks the genitive case with indefiniteness ('a far …'); the genitive usually links it to a preceding noun or follows a preposition.

1.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and indeed / and already' — wa- ('and') joined to qad, a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that something has certainly and already happened.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to the particle qad. With a past-tense verb, qad emphasizes that the action has truly and already taken place ('has indeed …'); with a present-tense verb it can instead mean 'sometimes / may'. It is a fixed particle with no case ending.

2.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
2.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

3.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
3.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
4.root: — (preposition)

5.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
5.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
5.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

7.meaning: 'In the unseen' — the preposition 'in/by' with 'the unseen': that which is hidden from perception, beyond what the senses can reach (such as Allah, the angels, and the Hereafter). It denotes the realm one cannot directly observe yet may affirm.
7.grammar: A preposition bi- joined to a definite masculine singular noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition — hence 'in the unseen'. The article al- makes it 'the unseen' as a known whole rather than 'an unseen thing'.
7.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — being hidden, absent from sight

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: Far, distant, or remote — in space, time, or figuratively (as in being far from the truth or from guidance).
10.grammar: An adjective in the intensive/quality paradigm. The -in ending marks the genitive case with indefiniteness ('a far …'); the genitive usually links it to a preceding noun or follows a preposition.

2.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
2.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
2.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

3.meaning: 'And between'. A connective word meaning 'and between / and amid', used to mark the space, relationship, or distinction lying among two or more parties.
3.grammar: The word bayna ('between') with 'and' in front. It is an adverb of place that always leads into what follows, so it ends in a fixed -a and is normally paired with a following noun or pronoun ('between … and …').
3.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinctness, 'between'

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: They crave or have an appetite for — to desire eagerly, to long for something pleasurable, especially food.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb (form VIII), third-person masculine plural. The ya-...-ūna frame means 'they (men) desire'; the final -ūna marks the plain indicative ('do / are doing').

6.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
6.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

10.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
10.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
10.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

11.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
11.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

12.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
12.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: 'Doubt / uncertainty.' A noun for the wavering state of mind in which one is unsure and cannot settle on what is true — the opposite of firm certainty.
14.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('a doubt / some doubt'). The genitive -i is the form taken after a preposition — typically conveying 'in doubt' or 'of doubt.'
14.root: ش-ك-ك (sh-k-k) — to doubt, be uncertain, waver
